parties:
Srizony Bangladesh represented by its Dr. M. Harun-or-Rashid, Chairman of Srizony Bhaban------------Petitioner
Vs

full_judgment:
Md Mozibur Rahman Miah, J: At the instance of the petitioner, Srizony Bangladesh in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 577 of 2022, this Rule was issued calling upon the opposite-parties to show cause as to why the order No. 4 dated 15-3-2023 passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka in the said Arbitration Miscellaneous Case replacing the arbitrator nominated and appointed by the petitioner under section 12 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. At the time of issuance of the Rule, this court also stayed the operation of the impugned order passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 577 of 2022 for a period of 3(three) months. Aside from that, on the date of issuance of the Rule, the learned District Judge, Dhaka was directed to appear before this court on 18-6-2023 to explain under what authority he replaced the arbitrator nominated by the petitioner named, Mr Justice Moyeenul Islam Chowdury, former Judge of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, High Court Division with one, Mr Dilip Kumar Bhowmick, Retired District and Sessions Judge. However, that very order was challenged by the learned District Judge before the Appellate Division by filing a civil petition for leave to appeal No. 1654 of 2023 and the learned Judge-in-Chamber by order dated 7-6-2023 stayed the operation so far as it relates to the appearance of the learned District Judge, Dhaka before this court though directed the learned District Judge to give explanation on the issue on 18-6-2023, the date fixed for his appearance before this court. Then as per the said direction made by the Appellate Division, the learned District Judge submitted an explanation before this court through the learned Registrar General, Supreme Court of Bangladesh. 

 3. The salient facts leading to issuance of the instant Rule are: The present petitioner entered into a contract through signing a participation agreement on 30-12-2002 with the opposite-party No. 2, Infrastructure Development Company Limited (briefly, IDCOL) on 30-12-2002 for supplying, installing and commissioning photovoltaic Solar Home System (shortly, SHS) in the under.- privileged areas of Bangladesh and under the said contract, the opposite-party No. 2 was supposed to provide grants and loans to the households so that the individual household may be able to purchase the said SHS in affordable price. The household was supposed to pay monthly installment against such 5H5 facilities under the agreement prepared and provided by IDCOL, the opposite-party No. 2 where the petitioner was supposed to collect the said monthly installment from the household on behalf of the opposite-party No. 2. Subsequently, the participation agreement dated 30-12-2002 was amended on 5-8-2012 and 13-11-2016 as of 3rd and 4th amendments. In view of the said agreement and amendments made thereafter, the petitioner implemented the said project for the opposite-party No. 2 with full satisfaction but it most illegally refused to pay the investment cost and expenses incurred by the petitioner in executing the said project and further created a undue pressure upon the petitioner and made various demands to pay alleged outstanding amount to the opposite-party No. 2. For that, the petitioner tried to resolve the dispute in all possible amicable ways but ultimately failed and in order to resolve the dispute, the petitioner finding no other alternative then issued an arbitration notice on 22-8-2022 upon the opposite-party No. 2 asking it to appoint their arbitrator within a period of 30(thirty) days from the date of receipt of the copy of the arbitration notice by appointing Mr Justice Moyeenul Islam Chowdhury, former Judge of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, High Court Division as its arbitrator. Since the opposite-party No. 2 upon receiving the said notice did not appoint any arbitrator to resolve the dispute as per the terms and conditions so provided in section 9.02 of article IX of the participation agreement dated 30-12-2002 (Annexure-`B' to the civil revision), the petitioner then compelled to file an application under section 12 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka seeking prayer for appointing arbitrator for opposite-party No. 2 which then gave rise to Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 577 of 2022 and the learned District Judge, Dhaka then fixed on 17-1-2023 for admission hearing (গ্রহণযোগ্যতা শুনানী) and ultimately it was admitted on that date vide order No. 2. The learned District Judge then took up the said case for hearing on 15-3-2023 and disposed of the same by appointing Mr Dilip Kumar Bhowmick, Retired District and Sessions Judge for the petitioner replacing the arbitrator so appointed by the petitioner, Mr Justice Moyeenul Islam Chowdhury and appointed Mr Md Nuruzzaman, Retired District and Sessions Judge for the opposite-party No. 2. 

 10. In this regard, the learned counsel has also placed his reliance in a decision of the Supreme Court of India held in the case of National Agricultural Co-op. Marketing Federation India Ltd. vs Gains Trading Ltd. reported in an online version "Manupatra" and submits that, in the said judgment, it has also been held that, even any clause of arbitration comes to an end and if the contract containing such arbitration agreement is abrogated yet the dispute among the parties has to be resolved through arbitration and that very proposition has also been affirmed in the decision delivered by the Supreme Court of India which has also been published in the online version "Manupatra" in the case of Kvaerner Cementation India Ltd. vs Bajranglal Agarwal and others and relying on those two decisions, the learned counsel finally prays for making the Rule absolute setting aside the impugned judgment and order. 

 15. The learned counsel further contends that, since the notice of the Arbitration Miscellaneous Case had not been served upon this opposite-party so it could not defend its position by filing written objection in the Arbitration Miscellaneous Case before the court of learned District Judge, Dhaka. 

 16. In reference to the provision laid down in section 3 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, the learned counsel next contends that, since there has been an overriding clause therein so this opposite-party is duty bound to realize its dues from the petitioner only in accordance with the respective provision of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 not through resolving the dispute in the arbitration proceeding and since by way of amendment, the participation agreement dated 30-12-2002 has been abrogated so the learned District Judge has committed apparent illegality in disposing of the Arbitration Miscellaneous Case by appointing arbitrator for the petitioner and the opposite-party No. 2. 

 22. The learned senior counsel for the opposite-party No. 2 also contends that, since the opposite-party did not get notice of the Arbitration Miscellaneous Case, it could not contest the said Case but from order No. 3 dated 13-2-2023, we don't find any support of the said submission because the said order depicts that the notice had duly been served upon the opposite-party No. 2. 

 24. For that obvious reason, we directed the learned District Judge, Dhaka to explain under what authority he changed the name of the arbitrator nominated by the petitioner directing him to appear before this court as we find from various civil revision that he deliberately committed such wrong for which both the parties to a Miscellaneous Case filed under section 12 of the Act are being aggrieved and kept on filing two sets of civil revisions impugning single judgment passed by him burdening this court which appears unusual. However, his appearance has been stayed by the Appellate Division directing him to give an explanation on that issue which he did. 

 27. Though the learned senior counsel for the opposite-party No. 2 relied on the decision reported in 57 DLR 734 but on going through it, we find the same to be totally inapplicable in the instant case. Because, in the cited decision, the order passed by the trial court staying a suit basing on an application filed under section 10 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 has been upheld enabling the parties to the dispute to resolve the same through Arbitration which rather supports the case of the petitioner here. 

 29. Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute however without any order as to costs and the case is sent back on remand to the learned District Judge, Dhaka. 

 30. The impugned judgment and order dated 15-3-2023 passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 577 of 2022 is thus set-aside. 

 31. The learned District Judge, Dhaka is hereby directed to dispose of the Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 577 of 2022 keeping in mind the above discussion and observation retaining the name of the arbitrator so nominated by the petitioner namely, Mr Justice Moyeenul Islam Chowdhury, former Judge of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, High Court Division and to appoint the arbitrator for the opposite-party No. 2 afresh which he is only authorized to do within a period of 30(thirty) days from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment.
